01 · Getting set up · Target 15 minutes

Your accounts & connections

Do these four steps in order. Email and calendar are optional.

1

Join your ESCP ChatGPT Edu workspace

  1. Open your ESCP inbox. Search for “Your access to ChatGPT EDU” from the ESCP GenAI team. Open the school’s activation link.
  2. At the OpenAI sign-in screen, click Continue with Google. Choose your @edu.escp.eu Google account. Complete any sign-up questions yourself.
  3. In ChatGPT ↗, click your profile icon. Choose ESCP Business School EDU in the workspace list.
  4. Check that ESCP Business School EDU appears in the profile menu before continuing.

No invitation? Use the ESCP GenAI page ↗ or email genai@escp.eu ↗. Edu is your school workspace; you do not need to buy Pro.

Show me: Choose the ESCP Edu workspace

Screenshot from the workshop rehearsal. Your account may show slightly different labels.

2

Connect email & calendar · optional

  1. In ChatGPT’s left sidebar, click Plugins ↗. Search for Gmail. Open the official Google mail plugin.
  2. Click Install or Connect. Choose the Google account you want to use. Read the requested permissions and continue only if you are comfortable with them.
  3. Return to Plugins. Search for Google Calendar and repeat the connection steps.
  4. To check or remove a connection, click Profile → Settings → Integrations → Plugins. Open the plugin to manage its account and permissions.

Prefer to skip this? Use the fictional tasks in the dashboard section ↗. For a Microsoft account, look for Outlook Email and Outlook Calendar instead.

Show me: Find a tool in the plugin directory

Screenshot from the workshop rehearsal. Your account may show slightly different labels.

3

Create your GitHub account & project

  1. Open github.com/signup ↗. Use Continue with Google or enter your email. Choose a username and finish the on-screen verification.
  2. Open New repository ↗. Under Owner, select your username. In Repository name, type my-ai-project.
  3. Select Public. Turn on Add a README file. Click Create repository. Keep this tab open.

Use this public repository only for the fictional game or company website. Your personal dashboard stays in ChatGPT Sites.

Show me: Create a public repository

Screenshot from the workshop rehearsal. Your account may show slightly different labels.

4

Connect that repository to ChatGPT Edu

  1. Go back to ChatGPT. Click your profile and check ESCP Business School EDU. Open Plugins ↗ and search GitHub.
  2. Open the official GitHub plugin. Click Install or Connect, then continue to GitHub and sign in.
  3. Review the consent screen. It may ask to verify your identity and read your GitHub-registered email addresses. This is account metadata, not access to your email inbox.
  4. When GitHub asks which repositories to allow, select Only select repositories. Choose my-ai-project, then click Install & Authorize.
  5. Return to ChatGPT. Click Profile → Settings → Integrations → Plugins → GitHub. Under Uses, click GitHub and check the connected account. Use Try in chat when available.

Already connected? Open GitHub’s Installed GitHub Apps ↗, find the OpenAI connector, click Configure and add your new repository. If school settings block writing, use the manual upload steps in the GitHub section.

Show me: Choose only your workshop repository

Screenshot from the workshop rehearsal. Your account may show slightly different labels.

02 · Connect tools & make a dashboard

A dashboard you would actually use

Tools give ChatGPT access to a task, such as reading a calendar. Sites turns your idea into an interactive app.

Try the fictional Focus desk dashboard ↗
1

Get a short task list

  1. Open a new chat in your ESCP Edu workspace.
  2. If you connected Gmail and Calendar, paste the prompt below. Review the task list and correct any dates before using it.
With connected tools

WHATFind my school email action items from the last 7 days and calendar deadlines for the next 7 days.

HOW · format & styleMake a short table: task, due date, source link. Mark missing dates as unknown.

WHYHelp me choose what to do next. Read only; do not send or change anything.

Or copy these fictional tasks
Finish marketing slide — today, 17:00 — 25 min
Book club meeting room — tomorrow, 12:00 — 10 min
Read strategy case — Friday, 18:00 — 45 min
Prepare group agenda — tomorrow, 10:00 — 15 min
Group project check-in — today, 16:00
2

Choose a style & build with Sites

Choose one style. The prompt below updates for you.

  1. In the same chat, type @ and choose Sites. Paste the prompt below and send it.
  2. Open the Site preview. Click the time filters and mark one fictional task done. Ask for one improvement.
  3. Keep the Site private / only you if it contains personal tasks. Publish only after checking the audience shown in the sharing dialog.
Build prompt

WHATUse @Sites to make a private dashboard from this checked task list.

HOW · format & styleUse [STYLE]. Add Today, This week, a 30-minute filter and Done buttons.

WHYHelp me choose my next task quickly. Keep personal data private.

This first version uses a checked snapshot. It does not automatically stay in sync with your inbox.

03 · An introduction to GitHub

Make something. Share the link.

A repository stores your project. A commit records a change. GitHub Pages serves your HTML as a public website.

1

Choose a game or fictional company

Open a new ChatGPT chat. Pick one prompt. Replace [STYLE] with a style you like.

Option A · memory game

WHATMake a simple memory-pairs game.

HOW · format & styleUse [STYLE]. Add a timer, score and Restart. Give me one downloadable index.html file.

WHYI want a fun game I can share with classmates.

Option B · fictional company

WHATMake a website for a fictional coffee brand called Orbit Coffee.

HOW · format & styleUse [STYLE]. Add a short pitch, three products and a working menu filter. Give me one index.html file.

WHYI want to show how a simple idea becomes an interactive website.

  1. Download the index.html file ChatGPT returns. Open it in your browser.
  2. Try the main button or game. Ask ChatGPT to fix anything that does not work.
2

Ask ChatGPT to save it to GitHub

  1. In the same chat, type @ and choose GitHub. Keep the finished HTML attached or in the conversation.
  2. Replace the two placeholders below with the GitHub username and repository you created in setup. Send the prompt.
  3. Open the repository link ChatGPT returns. Check that project/index.html appears and the content is your fictional project.
Publish prompt

WHATPublish this fictional project to [USERNAME]/[REPOSITORY] on GitHub.

HOW · format & styleCreate a new project/index.html on main. Keep other files unchanged and return the public GitHub Pages URL. Ask before overwriting anything.

WHYI want classmates to open the website without signing in.

The connection can submit files only when your workspace permits that tool. Ask it to confirm the actual commit and URL. Enable Pages once using the next step.

3

Turn on GitHub Pages once

  1. Open your repository. In its top menu click Settings. In the left sidebar, under Code and automation, click Pages.
  2. Under Build and deployment, set Source to Deploy from a branch.
  3. Under Branch, select main and /(root). Click Save.
  4. Wait for deployment, then refresh this Pages screen. Click Visit site. If the file is in project/index.html, add /project/ to the repository’s site URL.
  5. Open the link in a private/incognito window. Confirm it works without signing in.
Show me: Select main and /(root) for Pages

Screenshot from the workshop rehearsal. Your account may show slightly different labels.

GitHub Pages is public. Anyone can open or forward the link. Publish fictional content only. Official Pages help ↗

If the connection is blocked: upload the HTML yourself
  1. Open the repository’s Code tab. Click Add file → Upload files.
  2. Choose the index.html file. Under the commit message, select Commit directly to the main branch, then click Commit changes.
  3. Follow the Pages setup above. A root index.html opens at https://USERNAME.github.io/REPOSITORY/.
Show me: Upload index.html, then commit

Screenshot from the workshop rehearsal. Your account may show slightly different labels.

04 · Research with Perplexity

Tom · proposal to refine

Find evidence you can use

One question. Three findings. Check one original source.

  1. Open Perplexity ↗ and click the question box.
  2. Replace [our question] below. Submit the prompt.
  3. Click a numbered source beside a claim. Check its date, author and whether it supports that claim.
  4. Tell a partner which finding you trust and what remains uncertain.
Research prompt

WHATFind out [our question].

HOW · format & styleGive me three findings with links to recent primary sources. Flag one uncertainty.

WHYHelp me make a decision I can justify.

05 · Create a presentation

Iulia Korneeva · proposal to refine

Turn notes into a clear story

A prompt describes this task. A skill packages reusable instructions. A tool performs an action.

  1. Open ChatGPT ↗. Paste a short set of notes.
  2. Paste the prompt below. Replace the two placeholders.
  3. Read the proposed slide messages first. Correct the story before polishing the design.
  4. Ask for one change and compare the result. Iulia will demonstrate the chosen presentation tool or skill.
Presentation prompt

WHATTurn these notes into three editable slides for [audience].

HOW · format & styleUse a clean visual style, one message per slide and short text. Use only my notes.

WHYHelp the audience understand [key idea].
